LOOK: The Davao City Police Office reported more or less 7,500 people gathered at San Pedro Square in Davao City as of 6 p.m. on Sunday, September 21, for the “Pray for the Philippines and the Release of Former President Rodrigo Duterte” movement, a prayer rally that drew large crowds despite intermittent rain showers.

DCPO acting director Police Colonel Mannan Caracas Muarip, who personally conducted a security inspection and launched aerial monitoring using drone technology to ensure real-time crowd assessment and coordination, reported that the event remained peaceful and orderly, with security operations.

Aside from 100 roasted beef and a massive crocodile cake, the organizers also prepared a roasted crocodile. The crowd continues to line up for the packed lunch and dessert. 

📸: Ivy Tejano | MB

🇵🇭 Violence erupts in Philippines as furious anti-corruption protesters clash with cops

Sep 21,2025

Tensions escalated in the Philippine capital city of Manila as thousands of protesters took to the streets and clashed with police in an anti-corruption demonstration on Sunday (September 21).  

Protesters planned to hold their rally in front of the presidential palace, but were barred by the police, which resulted in violence as people tore down barricades on the streets. 

Allegations of mismanagement of the government's flood control projects have been in the spotlight in recent months during the country's monsoon season, which has inundated towns and cities despite spending over 545 billion pesos ($9.54 billion) on flood control since 2022.
